_comment: Department of Basic Education Grade 10 Mathematics P1 (algebra, patterns, finance, functions and probability), November 2019 national common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers transcribed from the rendered pages of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf); the text layer does not hold usable equations. Notation:
^ for powers, sqrt() for roots, a/b for fractions, decimal commas as printed. memo_answer is the
guideline's final answer and memo_working its working (tick marks and mark descriptors left out).
The guideline is bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. Graphs and diagrams are described
in brackets in the question text. The information sheet printed with the paper is not transcribed.
Both PDFs were obtained from the Eastern Cape Department of Education exam archive (source_url); the
page headers read 'DBE/November 2019' and 'CAPS - Grade 10', i.e. this is the national DBE paper
written in the province. The question paper is a scan with no text layer.
FORMAT: 100 marks, 2 hours, seven compulsory questions (Q1 13, Q2 19, Q3 16, Q4 10, Q5 14, Q6 16, Q7 12).

questions.text: During a fundraising event, only R10, R20 and R50 notes were collected. In the final count, there were twice as many R20 notes as there were R50 notes, and 15 more R10 notes than R50 notes. If R10 150 was collected in total, determine the number of R10, R20 and R50 notes that were collected.
questions.memo_answer: R10 notes = 115 ; R20 notes = 200 ; R50 notes = 100
questions.memo_working: let the number of R50 notes be x: R10 notes x + 15, R20 notes 2x; 10(x + 15) + 20(2x) + 50x = 10 150; 100x = 10 000; x = 100

questions.text: Write down the next term in the pattern.
Write, in terms of x, the formula for Tn, the general term of the pattern.
questions.memo_working: Tn = mn + c with m = x + 2; 2x + 1 = x + 2 + c gives c = x - 1; Tn = (x + 2)n + (x - 1)
questions.memo_note: The guideline's working uses the second term (4x + 5 = 3x + 6 + q) for the same constant q = x - 1.

questions.text: If the value of the 13th term of the pattern is 95, calculate the value of x.
If x = 5, determine the largest value of n for which Tn < 158.

questions.text: Calculate the height (H), in cm, of the tower.

questions.context: QUESTION 4 | 4.1 Peter wants to buy a computer costing R7 950, on a hire-purchase agreement. The conditions of the agreement are: • Peter must pay a deposit of 25% of the purchase price. • Interest is charged at 15% per annum simple interest on the balance. • He must also pay a compulsory monthly insurance premium of R70,75. • The balance is to be settled in monthly instalments.
questions.text: Calculate the balance after Peter pays the deposit.
If the balance is to be paid off in 24 months, calculate Peter's total monthly instalment.

questions.context: 4.2 The table below shows the cost of one British pound and one US dollar in South African rand. [England: Pound (£), R23,43; USA: Dollar ($), R14,58]
questions.text: It costs £55 to fill a car with 80 litres of petrol in England. How much will it cost to fill up with the same quantity of petrol if you were paying in South African rand?
An English visitor to the USA notices a car on sale for $5 500. A similar vehicle in England costs £3 500. In which country is the car more expensive? Justify your answer with relevant calculations.
questions.memo_answer: The car is more expensive in England.

questions.context: 7.2 A circular spinner is divided into 12 equal sectors. Each sector is numbered from 1 to 12. When spun, the spinner has an equal chance of stopping at any of the numbers 1 to 12.
questions.text: For any random spin, what is the probability that the spinner will stop at a square number?

The number that the spinner stopped at after the first spin was recorded. The number that the spinner stopped at after the second spin was also recorded. Calculate the probability that the sum of the two numbers at which the spinner stopped is greater than 2.
